hero.title: Sleep Guardian
hero.introA: Young adults know they should put their phone down — yet they don't. I designed a custom research app and a controlled experiment to find out
hero.introB: when willpower has already run out.
hero.roleValue: Lead Researcher · App Developer · Interaction Designer

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.title: A brain at war with itself — every night
problem.p1b: is distinct from simply going to bed late. It describes users who are
problem.p1c: yet keep scrolling — a state where cognitive resources are depleted and System 1 (fast, automatic, habit-driven) completely dominates System 2 (slow, rational, self-controlling).
problem.p2: Existing interventions — screen-time limits, hard locks, blunt warnings — trigger psychological reactance. Users dismiss them reflexively, because the intervention itself is operating at the wrong cognitive level.
problem.quote: "How can a notification design interrupt mindless scrolling without triggering the same automatic dismissal it's trying to prevent?"
problem.stat1desc: of university students report habitually sleeping fewer than 7 hours
problem.stat2desc: average delay between intended and actual sleep time among participants in pilot interviews
problem.stat3desc: pilot semi-structured interviews (ORID method) confirmed that existing tools are bypassed or ignored

framework.heading: Theoretical Framework
framework.title: Dual-Process Theory as design logic
framework.introA: The core design claim: to interrupt in-bed procrastination, interventions must operate on
framework.introB: that correspond to different cognitive mechanisms — not just repeat the same blunt warning.

threat.title: Threat Appeal
threat.desc: Presents health-risk information (e.g. cardiovascular load from sleep deprivation) to trigger rational risk assessment and protective motivation. Based on Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model (1992).
threat.example: "Warning: abnormal resting heart rate detected — continued sleep deprivation significantly increases cardiovascular risk."

empathy.title: Empathy Appeal
empathy.desc: Uses warm, non-judgmental language rooted in self-compassion theory (Neff, 2003) to reduce anxiety, lower psychological reactance, and gently invite rest rather than demand it.
empathy.example: "You made it through a tough day — this time belongs to you. Let yourself rest."

friction.title: Design Friction
friction.descA: Embeds a simple math problem (e.g. "Enter 3+4 to dismiss") directly in the notification UI. Does not rely on persuasion — it
friction.descB: a cognitive mode switch, interrupting the automatic scrolling loop. Based on Cox et al. (2016).
friction.interactionDesc: User must solve a math equation and type the correct answer before the notification can be dismissed.

experiment.heading: Experiment Design
experiment.title: A 3×3 mixed design in real bedrooms
experiment.introA: Rather than bringing participants into a lab (which would destroy ecological validity for a bedtime behavior), I ran the controlled experiment
experiment.counterB: — each participant experiences all 4 modality conditions in a balanced order (R1–R4), controlling for order effects and carryover effects across the within-subjects factor.
experiment.proto1desc: 21:00–03:00 only. App is time-locked — participants can only open it in their actual bedtime window.
experiment.proto2desc: Each notification is separated by a 3-minute re-immersion period, allowing participants to re-enter mindless scrolling before the next interruption.
experiment.proto3desc: First 3 minutes: no notification delivered. Allows System 1 to fully engage before any intervention — maximizing ecological validity.
experiment.proto4desc: 16 per group. Power analysis via G*Power (Faul et al., 2007) informed the sample for detecting a medium interaction effect in the 3×3 mixed ANOVA.

instrument.heading: The Research Instrument
instrument.title: Sleep Guardian — built from scratch with AI-assisted development
instrument.intro: Standard off-the-shelf apps can't run this kind of controlled experiment. I built Sleep Guardian using React Native / Expo — a custom experimental platform with four core modules.
instrument.mod1desc: Participants log into their own Instagram accounts inside the app, then scroll a real feed. This is the experimental "stimulus" — genuine, naturalistic mindless scrolling, not a fake interface.
instrument.mod2desc: Each participant receives a unique experience code that maps to their assigned notification type group (T/E/F) and their specific modality order (R1–R4). The system loads the correct counterbalanced sequence automatically.
instrument.mod3desc: Two objective behavioral metrics recorded automatically in background:
instrument.ndlDesc: — time from notification appearance to dismissal (ms).
instrument.pscDesc: — number of swipes after each notification, measuring residual mindless scrolling.
instrument.mod4desc: After all 4 notifications, the app displays a session summary screen (Session ID + behavioral data). Participants screenshot this for triangulation, then complete the post-test questionnaire (PAD, TAM, UEQ-S) via embedded WebView with notification screenshots as recall cues.

measures.heading: Measurement Battery
measures.title: Six validated instruments + two objective metrics
measures.bpsDesc: Confirms participant has moderate-to-severe in-bed procrastination tendency (Kroese et al., 2014; α=0.92)
measures.bscsDesc: Individual differences in self-regulation as covariate (Tangney et al., 2004)
measures.reiDesc: Baseline cognitive style — System 1 vs System 2 preference (Epstein et al., 1996)
measures.ndlDesc: Milliseconds from notification appearance to user dismissal — objective measure of interruption effectiveness
measures.pscDesc: Number of swipes after each notification — measures residual mindless scrolling behavior
measures.padDesc: Pleasure / Arousal / Dominance — measures emotional response to each notification type × modality (Mehrabian & Russell, 1974)
measures.tamDesc: Perceived Usefulness (PU) + Behavioral Intention (BI) — ease-of-use excluded due to design friction's intentional cognitive cost (Davis, 1989)
measures.ueqsDesc: Pragmatic + Hedonic quality — overall app experience assessment with minimal cognitive load (Laugwitz et al., 2008)

rq.heading: Research Questions & Hypotheses
rq.title: What we're testing
rq.rq1q: Do the three notification types differ in their ability to interrupt in-bed procrastination?
rq.rq1pred: Predicted: Design Friction will produce the lowest Post-notification Scroll Count, as it forces behavioral interruption independent of user motivation.
rq.rq2q: Do audiovisual modalities differ in Notification Dismissal Latency and emotional arousal?
rq.rq2pred: Predicted: Visual+Audio combined will produce the shortest dismissal latency due to highest sensory salience.
rq.rq3q: Is there a significant interaction between notification type and audiovisual modality?
rq.rq3pred: Predicted: Specific combinations (e.g. Threat Appeal × Visual+Audio; Design Friction × Audio only) will produce amplified interruption effects beyond main effects alone.
rq.rq4q: Do individual traits (BPS severity, prior app experience) moderate intervention effectiveness?
rq.rq4pred: Predicted: Heavy procrastinators and those with prior tool experience will show greater reactance to Threat Appeal, and better compliance with Empathy Appeal or Design Friction.
rq.statsB: Primary analysis via 3×3 Mixed ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons. If individual traits show significant moderation, elevated to Mixed ANCOVA with BSCS and BPS as covariates. All analyses in IBM SPSS.

status.heading: My Contribution & Current Status
status.title: What I've built so far
status.item1desc: 50+ peer-reviewed sources across sleep science, HCI, persuasive design, and dual-process theory. Identified the research gap: no prior in-situ study has compared threat, empathy, and friction interventions within a controlled audiovisual modality design.
status.item2desc: Semi-structured interviews using the ORID framework. Surfaced three design implications: (1) soft vs. forced control preference split → validates all three intervention types; (2) audio cues effective at night → validates modality factor; (3) mindless scrolling as flow state → validates Instagram-feed simulation approach.
status.item3desc: Full experimental platform built in React Native / Expo. Implements Instagram-feed simulation, experience code dispatch, Latin Square counterbalancing (R1–R4), time-locked session window (21:00–03:00), automated behavioral data logging, and WebView survey integration.
status.item4desc: Designed the full notification stimulus set — text, visual assets, audio recordings, and the design friction math-input interface — with equivalence controls for duration and visual complexity across conditions.
status.item5desc: Recruitment and data collection completed: N=48 (16 per group), plus 45 qualitative interviews.
status.item6desc: Mixed ANOVA in SPSS completed; thesis defended on June 26, 2026. Headline findings: interventions moved subjective emotion strongly (η²p = .18–.29) while automatic scrolling barely changed; appeal-type differences concentrated in the audio-only channel; design friction showed a very large arousal effect against baseline (d = −1.282); and only the empathy group’s intention converted into actual behaviour (r = +.516).

hero.title: OpenHCI'25 | Oblivilight
hero.subtitle: Exploring AI Forgetting Mechanisms Through Tangible Interaction

challenge.title: Rapid Prototyping Challenge
challenge.desc: This fully functional physical prototype was conceived, designed, and built within an intensive OpenHCI workshop—demonstrating exceptional teamwork, rapid iteration, and innovative problem-solving under pressure.

concept.heading: The Core Concept
concept.desc: Oblivilight is a tangible interaction device that explores how AI systems can "forget" information. In an era of digital hoarding and privacy concerns, this project reimagines data deletion as a meaningful, ritual-like experience through physical interaction.

research.heading: User Research & Insights
research.desc: I led 11 user interviews on the emotional weight of digital memory. They surfaced one contradiction that reset the project: people want to confide in AI but fear being remembered permanently. That finding pushed us off the original AI-diary concept and onto active forgetting as the core experience, and I translated colour psychology into a system of 10 emotional light states.

flow.heading: Interaction Flow: Print → Review → Decide
flow.desc: A 3-step physical ritual to process and curate digital memories.
flow.step1desc: At the end of the day, Oblivilight synthesizes the user's interactions and prints a physical "memory receipt", bringing ephemeral digital data into the physical world.
flow.step2desc: The user holds the physical paper, reviewing the AI's interpretation of their day. This tangible format forces a slower, more deliberate reflection compared to scrolling on a screen.
flow.step3desc: The user makes a physical choice: keep the receipt in a journal (Save), or feed it back into the top of Oblivilight, where a built-in shredder destroys it—signaling the AI to permanently "forget" that data.

tech.heading: Technical Implementation
tech.intro: Building Oblivilight required integrating custom hardware with software logic within a 6-day sprint. The system relies on an Arduino microcontroller to orchestrate the interactions — my teammates led the hardware and AI model, while I focused on user research and interaction design.
tech.item1desc: Handles input/output logic and component synchronization.
tech.item2desc: Custom integration to format and print thermal receipts dynamically.
tech.item3desc: Hacked a commercial shredder to trigger via Arduino relay.
tech.item4desc: Laser-cut acrylic enclosure and 3D-printed internal mounts.

hero.title: Mù – A Multisensory Guide
hero.subtitle: Rebuilding the sensory relationship between people and Taiwan's endangered woods

overview.heading: Project Overview
overview.desc: While twelve native tree species in Taiwan are legally defined as precious woods, most urban visitors only encounter them as commodities. Mù is a multisensory guidance app and exhibition concept that turns abstract ecological loss into a rediscoverable experience. Using scent, sound, touch, and visual storytelling, it lets visitors feel endangered woods as living beings.
overview.card1desc: Engaging users beyond screens through curated soundscapes and localized scents.
overview.card2desc: Orchestrating a cohesive journey across the Domain of Sacred Trees to the Forest of Memories.
overview.card3desc: Translating complex conservation data into digestible, card-based tree profiles.

challenge.heading: The Challenge: Bridging the Awareness Gap
challenge.title: Why is conservation so hard to communicate?
challenge.desc: Illegal logging heavily affects Taiwan's first-grade timber species. However, for the general public, this issue feels distant. How do we make urban populations care about something they rarely see or interact with?
challenge.item1desc: People know trees are disappearing, but it remains a headline rather than an emotional connection.
challenge.item2desc: Traditional museum text panels cause fatigue and fail to evoke empathy for the environment.
challenge.coreQuote: "How can a multisensory, research-driven guide turn 'I know trees are disappearing' into 'I feel connected and want to protect them'?"

research.heading: Research & Insights Synthesis
research.intro: To ensure our solution was grounded in reality, we conducted a mixed-methods research approach, including desk research and a quantitative survey (n=23) focused on wood fragrance experiences. Testing our original sleep-pod concept against that data is what killed it — I led the pivot to building recognition for Taiwan’s 12 precious woods instead.
research.f1desc: 91.3% of respondents showed high interest in sustainability, but lacked basic knowledge of native woods.
research.f1insight: Insight: A micro-learning approach is essential.
research.f2desc: Survey revealed a strong preference for localized, point-based sniffing to avoid sensory overload.
research.f2insight: Insight: Scent must be controlled and localized.
research.f3desc: Feedback was perfectly split, dictating the need for a flexible UX architecture.

solutions.heading: Design Solutions & Interactions
solutions.s1desc: Accommodating different visitor mindsets. The home screen provides a structured narrative path across four themed "forest islands".
solutions.s2desc: Clear visual cues showing the distance to specific trees or zones, allowing spontaneous exploration based on user location.
solutions.s3desc: Syncing with physical installations. Prompting users to pause and listen to breathing soundscapes, rebuilding the "forest rhythm".
solutions.s4desc: Replacing long text panels with digestible, card-based UI communicating habitat altitude and conservation threats.

impact.heading: Impact & Recognition
impact.title: A scalable, ethical exhibition framework
impact.nomineeDesc: The concept was officially nominated for the UX Design Awards, validating the project's research methodology and its approach to a difficult environmental communication problem.

hero.title: Innoconnect | Hi-Life Gift Service Optimization
hero.subtitle: Revitalizing the Digital Gifting Experience for a Major Taiwanese Retail Chain
hero.roleSub: Team "Lai Yi Ka" (萊一咖) of 3 members

intro.title: InnoConnect+ 2024 Challenge
intro.desc: Gold Award, Hi-Life Track — InnoConnect+ 2024 National Service Innovation Competition (186 teams entered, 10 finalists). This project reimagined Hi-Life's "Send a Gift" (來送禮) O2O service through strategic gamification and social features that drove measurable increases in user engagement and conversion rates.

overview.heading: Project Overview
overview.desc: Hi-Life, one of Taiwan's largest convenience store chains, operates a "Send a Gift" (來送禮) service that allows customers to send gifts through their stores. Despite the convenience, the service suffered from low awareness, complex user flows, and punitive policies that discouraged repeat usage. Our mission was to transform this underutilized service into a compelling social gifting platform.

challenge.heading: The Challenge
challenge.title: Why Wasn't Hi-Life's Gift Service Succeeding?
challenge.desc: Through comprehensive user research and competitive analysis, we identified three critical pain points preventing the "Send a Gift" service from reaching its potential. These issues created friction at every stage of the user journey, from awareness to post-purchase experience.
challenge.item1desc: Most users were unaware the service existed. Marketing was minimal, leading to poor traffic and conversion.
challenge.item2desc: The gifting process required multiple steps, excessive form inputs, and lacked clear visual guidance.
challenge.item3desc: If a gift expired unclaimed, users had to pay the price difference to redeem it—discouraging gifting altogether.
challenge.insight: Users want gifting to feel spontaneous, social, and risk-free—not transactional and complex.

strategy.heading: The Strategy: Gamification + Social Gifting
strategy.desc: We devised a two-pronged approach: attract new users through viral gamified marketing, then convert them into active gifters through social features and simplified flows.
strategy.leanTitle: Evaluating the Business Value and Future Feasibility for Hi-Life (Lean Canvas)

solution1.heading: Solution #1: Psychological Test (心理測驗)
solution1.title: Driving Traffic Through Viral Gamification
solution1.desc: We created a personality-driven psychological test that matches users with coffee flavors based on their traits. This shareable, fun experience serves as a low-friction entry point to the gifting service, turning casual browsers into engaged users.

solution2.heading: Solution #2: Wishlist & Social Gifting (許願池)
solution2.title: Turning Gifting Into a Social Activity
solution2.desc: The Wishlist feature allows users to create and share gift requests with friends. Instead of guessing what someone wants, senders can browse their friends' wishlists and send meaningful gifts. Recipients can also send interactive gift cards, increasing engagement and virality.
solution2.feat1desc: Users curate gift requests that friends can easily fulfill.
solution2.feat2desc: Browse wishlists of friends and discover gift opportunities.
solution2.feat3desc: Recipients send shareable gift cards to encourage friends to send gifts.

solution3.heading: Solution #3: Flow Optimization & Policy Changes
solution3.title: Removing Friction, Eliminating Penalties
solution3.desc: We completely redesigned the gifting flow, focusing on the core value propositions for both givers and receivers, while optimizing offline delivery and point refund mechanisms to create a frictionless O2O experience.
solution3.deliveryDesc: We proposed a new delivery platform service, "Lai-Song-Li", which delivers "Send a Gift" items directly to recipients, significantly reducing their time cost. Givers enjoy discounted shipping rates, or they can opt for Hi-Life's partnered logistics (such as Taiwan Pelican Express and HCT Logistics) for diverse delivery options.
solution3.refundDesc: For expired and unclaimed gifts, we eliminated the punitive policy that required users to pay the price difference. Instead, we implemented a mechanism to "refund equivalent member points to the user's account." This optimization not only relieves the givers' anxieties but also leverages the rule that the app must be downloaded to use points, effectively boosting the app's open and retention rates.

validation.heading: Validation: Usability Testing (SUS & UEQ)
validation.desc: We conducted comprehensive usability testing using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) to measure the impact of our redesign. The results confirmed significant improvements in user willingness, satisfaction, and overall experience.
validation.susDesc: 90% of participants gave positive ratings; 37% scored in the highest grade (A-level). Low-scoring users cited slight complexity and a learning curve.
validation.ueqDesc: Attractiveness & Enjoyment ranked highest. Functionality scored above average with room for improvement. Overall UX rated at "Good" level.

impact.heading: Recognition & Impact
impact.title: Gold Award Winner & Measurable Business Impact
impact.awardDesc: Gold Award, Hi-Life Track — InnoConnect+ 2024 National Service Innovation Competition (186 teams entered, 10 finalists). The judges recognized the project's strategic gamification, user-centered design, and measurable impact on conversion metrics.
impact.engagementDesc: In the concept validation survey (n=19), 68% said the personality quiz would make them use Send-a-Gift, and 73% said it made them willing to try Hi Café — the growth loop worked in both directions.
impact.researchDesc: SUS scores ranged from 57.5 to 95 (n=19), with 90% of participants giving positive ratings and 37% reaching A-level usability.

gcce.venue: Accepted and Presented at 2025 IEEE GCCE, Osaka
gcce.title: An Experimental Study on the Effect of AI Voice Prominence on Users' Emotional Responses
gcce.challenge: As AI-generated speech becomes increasingly natural and pervasive in digital content, its emotional impact remains underexplored. This study investigates how the "prominence" of an AI voice (how foregrounded it is) affects user emotions across different media contexts.
gcce.m1desc: Evaluated 39 university students using both the quantitative Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM) scale and qualitative semi-structured interviews.
gcce.m2desc: Tested three levels of AI voice prominence: High (Podcasts), Medium (Travel Vlogs), and Low (Instagram background music).
gcce.m3desc: Employed descriptive statistics and one-way ANOVA to test the significance of emotional differences (Pleasure, Arousal, Dominance) across conditions.
gcce.findings: Quantitative results revealed that lower AI voice prominence significantly increases user pleasure and arousal. Specifically, low prominence (Instagram background) yielded the highest pleasure (M=3.59) and arousal (M=2.88). Interviews indicated that AI voices are more acceptable in humorous or informational content, but less preferred in emotionally expressive formats.
gcce.pubTitle: AI Voice Subjectivity and Interactive Product Design
gcce.figCaption: Fig 1. AI Voice Acceptance Framework detailing cognitive-emotional dynamics.
gcce.implications: Product designers must calibrate AI vocal prominence to content goals. Highlights the need for context-aware design: use human-like prosody for affective formats, neutral delivery for informational clips, and stylized/robotic speech for comedic effect.

ssim.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Music and Interactive Design for University Students: Exploring Needs and Skill-Based Variations in Music Creation Experience
ssim.challenge: While AI tools for music composition are proliferating, there is limited research focusing on AI-assisted education tailored to the specific needs of users with varying levels of prior domain experience.
ssim.m1desc: Conducted focus group interviews with two distinct groups of university students (aged 19-21): those with and without prior music composition experience.
ssim.m2desc: Implemented a modular end-to-end AI workflow utilizing source separation, AI vocal synthesis (Synthesizer V, ACE Studio), and rule-based auto-arrangement.
ssim.m3desc: Collected quantitative pre-post data across six dimensions: Fluency, Ideational, Flow, Originality, Quality, and Sociality.
ssim.findings: Both groups exhibited positive attitudes but vastly different needs. Novices showed the largest gains in ideation, flow, and originality. Experienced learners prioritized building personalized AI models and desired minimal instructor interference, favoring prompt-based keyword guidance. Novices relied heavily on pre-designed models and required more basic scaffolding.
ssim.figCaption: Fig 2. Modular AI workflow separating analysis, conditioning, and resynthesis.
ssim.implications: Proves the necessity of adaptive UI/UX in AI tools. Products must offer progressive disclosure: providing advanced model-building features and creative freedom for experts, while offering simplified, pre-designed templates for novices.

overview.heading: Project Overview
overview.desc: This comprehensive project transformed Fuhshyuan Foods (福瑄食品), a traditional Taiwanese peanut brittle manufacturer, through a complete brand redesign and modern e-commerce website. The goal was to bridge generational preferences by modernizing the brand's visual identity and digital presence while preserving its rich Hakka cultural heritage.
overview.part1desc: Cultural storytelling through modern packaging design inspired by Hakka traditions
overview.part2desc: User-centered e-commerce experience with improved navigation and conversion flow

brand.heading: Brand & Packaging Redesign
brand.subtitle: Revitalizing Traditional Taiwanese Peanut Brittle for Modern Consumers
brand.challengeDesc: Fuhshyuan Foods (福瑄食品) faced declining engagement with younger demographics. The traditional packaging design failed to communicate the product's cultural value and quality, positioning it as outdated rather than heritage-rich.
brand.pain1: Old packaging was sticky and inconvenient for modern consumption
brand.pain2: Visual identity failed to attract 18-35 age demographic
brand.pain3: Cultural heritage story was not effectively communicated

strategy.heading: The Strategy
strategy.narrativeDesc: The rebranding centered around the Hakka festival "Tian Chuan Ri" (天穿日 - Heaven's Birthday). The word "Yun" (韻) in Chinese means "rhyme" or "rhythm," but phonetically it also implies "good luck" and "fortune." This dual meaning transformed the peanut brittle from a simple snack into a culturally meaningful gift symbolizing blessings and prosperity.
strategy.pillar1desc: Anchored in Hakka "Tian Chuan Ri" festival traditions, making the product culturally significant
strategy.pillar2desc: Woodblock printing aesthetics combined with contemporary design principles
strategy.pillar3desc: Single-serve instant packs solving stickiness while creating gift-ready format

design.heading: Design Solution
design.f1desc: Traditional Hakka art style modernized with vibrant colors and clean typography
design.f2desc: Individual instant packs eliminate stickiness and improve portability
design.f3desc: Premium packaging suitable for festivals and cultural celebrations

web.subtitle: Modernizing the E-Commerce Experience
web.contextDesc: Following the successful brand redesign, the official website needed a complete overhaul to match the new brand identity and improve the user experience. The old website suffered from poor navigation, unclear product information, and low conversion rates.
web.mapDesc: I created a comprehensive functional map to reorganize the website's information architecture. This process helped identify user pain points and streamline the navigation structure for better discoverability and conversion.
web.uiDesc: The final UI design focused on three key pages: Homepage (brand story and featured products), About Brand (Hakka culture and company values), and Product Listing (intuitive browsing and filtering).
web.h1desc: Homepage hero section showcases Hakka culture and "Good Luck" concept
web.h2desc: Simplified menu structure with clear product categories and filters
web.h3desc: Responsive layouts optimized for smartphone shopping experience

outcome.heading: Outcome & Impact
outcome.subtitle: Recognition and Results
outcome.r1desc: Won 2nd Place in the Creative Culture Graduate Exhibition, recognizing excellence in cultural brand design and digital innovation.
outcome.r2desc: Successfully repositioned a traditional product for younger demographics while preserving cultural authenticity.
outcome.r3desc: Created a modern e-commerce platform that improved user experience and sales conversion.

hero.title: 2025 34th Times Young Creative Awards
hero.subtitle: Yung Ching Housing Employer Branding Campaign
hero.teamNames: Chi-Yun Chien, Po-Yu Chen, He-Chi Wang, Yun-Rou Chang

overview.title: Multi-Channel Employer Branding Campaign
overview.desc: A comprehensive campaign for Yung Ching Housing that reimagined job hunting as a "Career Gashapon" experience. The project won 3rd place nationally in the video category and had three additional works shortlisted across interactive and audio formats, demonstrating excellence in integrated creative strategy.

concept.heading: Core Concept
concept.quote: "Job hunting is like a Gashapon (Capsule Toy)."
concept.desc: We transformed the anxiety of job hunting into the anticipation and excitement of a capsule toy machine. Each "turn" represents a career choice, but unlike random luck, Yung Ching offers guaranteed value—making the metaphor both relatable and empowering.
concept.keyMessage: "True value isn't luck, it's choosing a worthy partner."

work1.title: Work 1: "Career Festival" (轉職慶典)
work1.concept: The main video features a visually striking capsule machine designed for fresh graduates. Inside the transparent capsules are symbolic "career charms"—including "50k Guaranteed Salary" and "Freedom from Contracts." The film uses warm, inviting cinematography to contrast the cold reality of typical job hunting, positioning Yung Ching as a trustworthy partner rather than a gamble.
work1.el4: Warm cinematography vs. cold job market contrast

work2.title: Work 2: "Career Takeoff" (轉動職涯)
work2.concept: An online interactive experience styled like a Line chatbot, where users "turn" a digital gashapon machine to receive "Career Subscription Passes"—a clever parody of Netflix's subscription model. Each "pass" unlocks different career benefits (training, mentorship, flexibility), gamifying the discovery of Yung Ching's employee value proposition.
work2.keyCopy: "Subscribe to your career, not just a job."

work3.title: Work 3: "Job Personality Test" (工作不靠運)
work3.concept: A shareable personality test that flips the interview script: "Don't just ask the interviewer, ask yourself." Users discover their workplace persona through playful questions, receiving personalized insights that match them with Yung Ching's culture. The viral format drives organic traffic while educating candidates about self-awareness in career planning.
work3.keyCopy: "Don't just ask the interviewer, ask yourself."

work4.title: Work 4: "The Right Turn" (這一轉，選對了)
work4.concept: An audio-only experience that uses sound design to simulate the tactile anticipation of turning a gashapon machine. The "click-click-click" rhythm mimics a heartbeat, building tension before the satisfying "pop" of success. The script cleverly uses first-person narration to make listeners feel like they're making their own career choice in real-time.

impact.heading: Campaign Impact & Recognition
impact.title: National Recognition Across Multiple Formats
impact.r1desc: Won 3rd Place nationally in the Video Category for "Career Festival," recognized among hundreds of submissions for creative excellence and strategic messaging in employer branding.
impact.r2desc: Three additional works shortlisted across Interactive and Audio categories, demonstrating versatility in creative execution and integrated campaign thinking.
impact.r3desc: Successfully balanced playful metaphor ("Gashapon") with serious employer value proposition, making recruitment messaging both memorable and effective.

insights.heading: Creative Insights
insights.i1desc: The "Gashapon" metaphor wasn't decoration—it was a strategic device to reframe job hunting anxiety as playful anticipation.
insights.i2desc: A single concept ("Career Gashapon") was adapted across 4 formats (video, web, audio), proving the power of flexible creative platforms.
insights.i3desc: The campaign prioritized candidate self-awareness and empowerment ("ask yourself") over hard-sell tactics, building trust and brand affinity.
